subject: Mid-quarter steer: prioritize critical-path deps and targeted scope shifts
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightPath - Tina Rivera <tina.rivera@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter steer: prioritize critical-path deps and targeted scope shifts

Team — quick mid-q note and asks ahead of next week’s QBR prep run. High level: we’re tracking OKRs but have two cross-cutting risks that, if unresolved, will materially push rollout dates and increase cost per inference. I want to propose a narrow, reversible scope shift we can run for the next 6 weeks and a short list of dependency asks (owners and deadlines below).

Snapshot (where we are)
- Latency OTK: 18% behind trajectory vs. target reduction (mainly 99th pct tail on long contexts)
- Throughput goal (dedicated): 90% plateau during peak; autoscale not absorbing short bursts
- Cost-per-token target: within 3% of plan, but margin risk if latency fixes use larger instance classes

Proposed narrow shift (objective: protect Q4 launch SLA and predictable unit economics)
1) Defer non-essential telemetry pipeline (feature: request-level debug traces) from midq to post-QBR. Keeps data we need for long-term debugging but reduces peak IO pressure on Dedicated nodes.
2) Prioritize micro-batching for long-context flows (client opt-in flag) instead of global default — rollback by feature flag.

Dependency asks (owners + requested dates) — please confirm commitments by EOD Wednesday 9/2:
- Marcus: quota raise and instance reservation change with cloud infra team (needed by 9/8) — ETA and any procurement blockers?
- Vanessa: coordinate CS and BrightPath on client opt-in messaging (content + rollout plan) — initial draft by 9/3.
- Karthik: short security review for request-level tracing removal (impact on audit trails and retention) — signoff or call by 9/4.
- Tessa: consolidate QBR slide section on risks & mitigations; I attached a working draft.

Attachments: midq_dependency_matrix.xlsx (matrix of tasks/owners), qbr_slide_draft_v1.pptx

My ask in one line: confirm who can own each dependency and whether any of these are showstoppers for you. I want to lock these asks in before the exec QBR rehearsal on Thurs.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

Irene — can take the cloud quota + reservation ask. Quick notes:
- I can get the initial quota bump approved by 9/6, but procurement (AcmeOps) needs a 48h lead for a reserved change; I’m opening the ticket now.
- If we move more traffic to larger instances temporarily we’ll see a 9–12% bump in infra cost; I’ll model the delta and attach numbers by 9/3.

Also calling out a potential blocker: our marketplace procurement discount tier resets on 9/15 — if procurement needs time, we may lose that pricing band for this billing cycle. Marcus will tag AcmeOps on the ticket and sync.

Marcus

Irene — quick security note after initial review: removing request-level traces reduces our retention surface but creates two questions for compliance: (1) how we reconstruct incidents for SOC2 post-incident, and (2) whether existing audit copies in S3 meet the retention policy if we pause ingestion.

I’ll convene a 30-min sync with security and compliance on Thu 9/2 at 10:00 PT to validate the temporary policy and sign off on the retention offset. If security can’t sign by 9/4 we should not pause telemetry ingestion.

I confirm: I can own the review and will share proposed language for QBR notes.

—Karthik
Director, Security Engineering
